basis: Renal cystic disease; hepatic cysts occupy liver in 80-99%, usually preserving function. Valve and aneurysmal lesions occur in <30%; hypertension is separately coded.
Congenital ureteral dilatation with reflux and obstruction; ureters belong to the renal axis.
Noninflammatory kidney disease with proteinuria and renal protein loss; edema and hypoalbuminemia do not establish another damaged organ.
Inherited calcium regulation disorder. Paresthesia and spasms are hypocalcemic symptoms; basal ganglia calcification occurs in <30%.
Protein-losing glomerular disease; steroid resistance does not establish an autoimmune mechanism across this heterogeneous group.
Growth hormone resistance and immune dysregulation define the syndrome; eczematoid dermatitis occurs in 2/3. Thyroiditis and celiac disease each occur in 1/9.
Neuronal heterotopia and developmental delay in 7/7; toe syndactyly in 5/7 and cleft palate in 4/7 establish common skeletal and oral malformations.
Pancreatic endocrine VIP excess causes the defining intestinal secretory dysfunction, achlorhydria and hypokalemia; this is not an infection.
TAP1 immunodeficiency commonly causes chronic destructive airway disease/bronchiectasis; granulomatous skin ulceration occurs in roughly 30-50%. Ear involvement is unquantified.
Dermatophyte infection of scalp or beard skin and hair.
Complex I deficiency with cardiomyopathy 4/4 and encephalopathy 3/4; myopathy 30-79%. Hepatic steatosis and blood abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Disease located in the aortic valve; no common direct injury outside the cardiovascular axis defines this umbrella.
Invasive Candida infection; affected compartments vary, with no specific organ damaged in most cases. Candidemia alone is not blood-cell disease.
HNRNPA1-associated motor neuron degeneration; denervation weakness does not establish primary muscle disease, and reported myopathy lacks a common frequency.
Hair and nail dysplasia with intellectual disability define the syndrome. Teeth and sweating are normal; hearing impairment occurs in 5-29%.
Left ventricular noncompaction is a structural cardiomyopathy; no extracardiac disease is established for this subtype.
Corpus callosum agenesis establishes CNS malformation. Facial cleft anatomy is unspecified, so oral or skeletal involvement cannot be assigned reliably.
Fungal infection directly inflames the stomach.
Compound sickling hemoglobinopathy. Extrahematologic damage varies substantially by partner variant; no additional organ meets the common-damage threshold across this group.
Progressive inherited ataxia and neural degeneration; cardiomyopathy and skeletal deformities are less consistent in the retained-reflex subtype, without established >=30% injury.
Hystrix-like ichthyosis and sensorineural hearing loss define HID. Keratitis is unquantified and is not established as a common defining feature of this subtype.
Neurodevelopmental disease; dermatitis 2/2, cataract/high myopia 1/1, scoliosis 1/1. PDA 1/1 omitted at cap; reported denominators are very small.
Inherited retinal cone dysfunction causes loss of red color discrimination.
Microsporidial intestinal infection causes chronic diarrhea and malabsorption; diarrhea is reported in 30-79%. Other organ infections are uncommon; immunodeficiency usually predates infection.
Developmental delay in 80-99%; ptosis/blepharophimosis in 80-99% and strabismus/nystagmus in 30-79%. Hair, skin and external ear features lack established functional injury.
